doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Transposing keys and accompanying singers
summary: He transposes automatically and picks out chord changes quickly for singers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What about changing keys for a different situation, if you’re backing up a singer or even yourself. Did you start to get this idea that the song is the same in any key, you just have to think of the one and the six and the two and the five and so forth. Did that start to sort of gel in your head?

Well I just automatically transfer it to any key. You know. And quickly pick out the chord changes and you know you had to do that with singers. Some singers just — they might sing in a different key the same song. But you know most of the singers knew what they wanted, what key they wanted to sing in.
Yeah instead of getting a singer who goes, “Well my first note is [hums]” and you have to sort of figure it out yourself.
